simple.meaning: מַצֶּבֶת (matstsebeth) is a Hebrew object word meaning “something stationary , i.e. a monumental stone ; also the stock of a tree.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 35:14. The surrounding context includes family line, offering, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַצֶּבֶת (H4678) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

timeline.evidenceText: Jacob set up a pillar in the place where he spoke with him, a pillar of stone. He poured out a drink offering on it, and poured oil on it.
Jacob set up a pillar on her grave. The same is the Pillar of Rachel’s grave to this day.

Now Absalom in his lifetime had taken and reared up for himself the pillar which is in the king’s valley, for he said, “I have no son to keep my name in memory.” He called the pillar after his own name. It is called Absalom’s monument, to this day.
